textbook: Clean textbook illustration of the front end of an adult dog tapeworm (Taenia ovis), composed diagonally: the SCOLEX — the knob-like holdfast head — sits large in the upper-left third of the frame, seen from a high three-quarter angle, and the long FLAT ribbon of its body trails away to the lower-right corner and runs out of the frame. The head carries FOUR cup-shaped muscular suckers spaced evenly around it like the four legs of a stool, 90 degrees apart, and ALL FOUR are visible — count them: TWO large round rimmed cups on the front of the head facing the viewer, each a shallow shadowed bowl with a thick smooth rim, PLUS one cup on the head's LEFT edge and one cup on the head's RIGHT edge, each seen at a glancing angle as a narrow rimmed oval that bulges out of the head's silhouette like a small ear. At the very apex of the head sits a SMALL rounded knob — the rostellum, clearly smaller than any single sucker — wearing TWO concentric circlets of tiny amber-brown thorn-shaped recurved hooks: an inner ring of slightly larger hooks and an outer ring of slightly smaller ones, each hook drawn individually as a slim curved claw, sharp-tipped — a crown of little claws, never petals or a flower rosette. Directly behind the head comes a short NARROW SMOOTH unsegmented neck, visibly thinner than the head; behind the neck the body becomes the strobila: a FLAT TAPE like a strip of tagliatelle pasta — wide and thin, its thin edge visible along the curve so the flatness is obvious — divided by crisp creases running straight ACROSS its width into rectangular segments (proglottids) joined end to end, the segments starting small near the neck and growing steadily wider and longer toward the lower-right, where the tape leaves the frame. The last, largest visible segment is drawn in partial cutaway, its interior filled with a dense mass of tiny pale-amber rounded eggs branching from a central channel, showing that each ripe segment is a self-contained egg package; the worm's interior elsewhere is plain soft tissue — the animal has no mouth and no gut, so the inside is simple. Above the scolex, a gently curved band of dusty pink-salmon intestinal lining (the dog's gut wall, with soft finger-like villi) arcs across the top-left corner, the scolex nestled against it with its suckers gripping. Colour legend: cream-ivory gently opalescent worm body, warmer buff-tan sucker rims, tiny amber-brown hooks, faintly rose-grey egg mass in the cutaway segment, muted dusty pink-salmon gut wall. Semi-flat vector-ish shading, thin clean outlines (not heavy black cartoon strokes), gentle soft shading with subtle dimensionality, every structure its own distinct soft colour fill, muted sophisticated slightly-desaturated educational palette, generous negative space around each structure so labels can attach, neutral dark-charcoal uncluttered background beyond the gut wall. Square 1:1, 1080x1080, the illustration's own background filling the whole frame edge-to-edge with NO black border, frame, vignette or letterbox bars. Absolutely NO text, letters, numbers, labels, scale bars, arrows or watermarks baked into the image.
